MAX INTERNALS / CONTEXT, THREAD, EXECUTOR

A shared context.
A scope on each thread.

Graph() does not require a Python worker thread. It needs a valid MLIR context on whichever thread calls it. Workers are chosen by other APIs for specific scheduling needs.

calling thread→context guard→Graph G1

01 / PYTHON THREADS AND MLIR

Graph needs an active context on its calling thread

The fused-attention example needs no Python worker to construct G1. The decorator makes construction work on the calling thread, including a background thread chosen elsewhere. ↗ fused_attention.py:41↗ graph.py:819

Watch the context object stay fixed while each thread’s scope reference changes. G1 appears in host-side IR storage.

    The module stores one default context and enters it on the importing thread, normally the main thread. The atexit handler balances this scope.

Three different things

_DEFAULT_MLIR_CONTEXT is a module-global Python reference to one MLIR Context object. Its native context stores uniqued types/attributes and dialect machinery. It does not mean “the current context of every thread.” ↗ _mlir_context.py:26↗ MLIRContext.h:43

mlir.Context.current is a property that reads the top of the calling thread’s context stack. Example: main → MLCTX0, W0 → None, W1 → C2 can all be true at the same instant. TLS means thread-local storage. ↗ IRCore.cpp:3455↗ IRCore.cpp:587

MLIRThreadPoolExecutor is a Python executor object. It schedules callables and wraps them with context activation. It neither is the context nor stores the graph IR itself. ↗ _mlir_context.py:89↗ _mlir_context.py:97

Does Graph ever start a different process?

For kernels/ source input, custom-package preparation can invoke mojo precompile in a separate compiler process to produce P1. That tool subprocess is distinct from a Python thread-pool worker. The context diagrams zoom into Graph’s calling thread and host-side IR; they do not depict the compiler subprocess’s internals. ↗ paths.py:178↗ run.py:74

What does @ mean?

This is a Python decorator, roughly Graph.__init__ = in_default_mlir_context(original_init). It returns a wrapper which checks the context, calls the original function and exits its scope. No submit, await or thread creation appears in the synchronous wrapper. ↗ _mlir_context.py:70↗ _mlir_context.py:82

Why does the default context exist?

Operations need a context for their IR types, attributes and dialects. A long-lived default keeps ordinary API calls convenient; the scoped helper also respects an explicit context supplied by a caller. An MLIR API that needs an implicit context can raise if none is active. ↗ IRCore.cpp:571↗ _mlir_context.py:55

Why thread-local current state?

Different host threads can be at different points in nested context/location/insertion scopes. Each thread needs its own active stack even when they refer to the same context object. The native binding implements this using a thread_local vector. ↗ IRCore.cpp:587↗ IRCore.cpp:598

Why balanced per-call scopes?

Worker threads do not inherit the importing thread’s MLIR stack. Entering and exiting around the job gives implicit MLIR APIs the needed environment and releases temporary TLS references before teardown. MAX’s source explicitly cites avoiding nanobind GIL/TLS teardown crashes; the module’s atexit handler balances the import-thread entry. ↗ _mlir_context.py:30↗ _mlir_context.py:33

Does sharing the context serialize graph edits?

No mutex is acquired by this Python helper. It supplies context scope; it is not a promise that arbitrary concurrent mutation of one Graph is safe. The native MLIR context has separate multithreading facilities, and caller-owned IR still has its own lifetime and mutation rules. ↗ _mlir_context.py:55↗ MLIRContext.h:50

02 / PYTHON THREADS AND MLIR

What the pool actually schedules

A pool is a scheduling tool. MAX adds a thin MLIR-scope wrapper to Python’s ThreadPoolExecutor. The base executor owns the queue, threads and Future delivery. ↗ _mlir_context.py:89

J1 moves from the submitting thread into a queue and W0. R1 returns through F1; the shared context stays in the same process.

Job returns R1 · all steps
  1. Wrap the submitted function

    E1.submit(fn,*args) delegates to the base executor with call_with_default_mlir_context as the scheduled function. fn and its arguments become that wrapper’s arguments.

    ↗ _mlir_context.py:97
  2. Create F1 and enqueue J1

    CPython creates Future F1 and a _WorkItem that retains the callable and its arguments. The queue receives J1; the caller receives F1. Diagram schedules are illustrative.

    ↗ thread.py:176↗ thread.py:179
  3. Start or reuse a worker

    _adjust_thread_count first looks for an idle worker. Otherwise it creates one if below max_workers. W0’s target is _worker, not Graph.__init__.

    ↗ thread.py:184↗ thread.py:198
  4. Dequeue and mark running

    W0 takes J1 and _WorkItem.run changes F1 to RUNNING unless it was cancelled. This worker, not the submitting thread, calls the wrapper.

    ↗ thread.py:93↗ thread.py:55
  5. Activate MLIR on W0

    The wrapper sees None and enters MLCTX0. The same shared context object now has a scoped reference on W0. It calls fn(*args,**kwargs).

    ↗ _mlir_context.py:44↗ _mlir_context.py:49
  6. Produce R1

    The submitted function returns a Python object. For example, build_graph returns G1; the actual PyTorch integration submits session.load and gets Model M1.

    ↗ thread.py:59↗ torch.py:488
  7. Exit scope before publishing result

    with _DEFAULT_MLIR_CONTEXT unwinds before the wrapper returns to _WorkItem.run. W0’s current stack returns to its earlier state.

    ↗ _mlir_context.py:50↗ IRCore.cpp:667
  8. Finish F1 and notify waiters

    _WorkItem.run calls F1.set_result(R1). Future stores the result, changes state to FINISHED and notifies its condition waiters. result() returns the same object reference.

    ↗ thread.py:65↗ _base.py:537↗ _base.py:428
  9. Reuse W0 for later jobs

    The worker loops back to get another work item. Idle workers can handle later submissions in this executor; max_workers limits worker count, not queue length.

    ↗ thread.py:90↗ thread.py:186
Job raises an exception · all steps
  1. Wrap the submitted function

    E1.submit(fn,*args) delegates to the base executor with call_with_default_mlir_context as the scheduled function. fn and its arguments become that wrapper’s arguments.

    ↗ _mlir_context.py:97
  2. Create F1 and enqueue J1

    CPython creates Future F1 and a _WorkItem that retains the callable and its arguments. The queue receives J1; the caller receives F1. Diagram schedules are illustrative.

    ↗ thread.py:176↗ thread.py:179
  3. Start or reuse a worker

    _adjust_thread_count first looks for an idle worker. Otherwise it creates one if below max_workers. W0’s target is _worker, not Graph.__init__.

    ↗ thread.py:184↗ thread.py:198
  4. Dequeue and mark running

    W0 takes J1 and _WorkItem.run changes F1 to RUNNING unless it was cancelled. This worker, not the submitting thread, calls the wrapper.

    ↗ thread.py:93↗ thread.py:55
  5. Activate MLIR on W0

    The wrapper sees None and enters MLCTX0. The same shared context object now has a scoped reference on W0. It calls fn(*args,**kwargs).

    ↗ _mlir_context.py:44↗ _mlir_context.py:49
  6. The callable raises

    Illustrative ValueError from fn. Exiting the with scope still pops MLCTX0; a failed job does not leave that temporary context entered on W0.

    ↗ _mlir_context.py:49↗ IRCore.cpp:667
  7. Store failure in F1

    _WorkItem.run catches BaseException and calls set_exception. F1 becomes FINISHED with an exception; it does not acquire a successful R1.

    ↗ thread.py:60↗ thread.py:61
  8. result() raises to the caller

    Future.result obtains the finished outcome. __get_result raises the stored exception. W0 can return to the queue loop after this task failure.

    ↗ _base.py:398↗ thread.py:93

Concrete input and output

Illustrative call: F1 = E1.submit(build_graph, "attention"). The queued function is call_with_default_mlir_context; its positional arguments are (build_graph, "attention"). _WorkItem also holds F1. It does not serialize or copy an entire graph into another process. ↗ _mlir_context.py:97↗ thread.py:47

If build_graph("attention") returns G1, then F1 retains G1 and F1.result() returns G1. If it raises ValueError, the Future stores that exception. This is a same-process thread handoff. ↗ _base.py:537↗ _base.py:552

Implementation boundary

Queue/thread/Future internals are shown from CPython v3.13.7 as a pinned reference. The MAX checkout selects Python 3.13 by default; this page does not claim to have measured the installed interpreter’s exact patch release. The MAX wrapper and callers use the checkout revision shown below. ↗ common.MODULE.bazel:189↗ thread.py:122

Why a pool rather than a new thread per call?

One executor can reuse idle workers, bound the number of active worker threads and expose results/errors through Futures. _adjust_thread_count and the worker loop implement reuse. Its SimpleQueue is not a bounded admission queue: max_workers does not cap pending submissions. ↗ thread.py:186↗ thread.py:154

Why a MAX-specific subclass?

A plain ThreadPoolExecutor does not know about MLIR’s native thread-local context stack. MAX overrides only submit so every submitted callable gets the correct per-call scope. Graph’s own decorator protects that constructor; the executor can protect an entire job containing other MLIR calls too. ↗ _mlir_context.py:89↗ graph.py:819

Does a Future make the caller nonblocking?

submit returns a Future without waiting for the result. Calling result() or leaving an executor with-block can still block. Actual speedup depends on the work and interpreter/native behavior; the existence of this wrapper proves no speedup by itself. ↗ _base.py:428↗ _base.py:647

03 / PYTHON THREADS AND MLIR

A real need: bridge a synchronous call into a second event loop

A worker solves the already-running-loop constraint here. This is the experimental tensor API’s _run helper, separate from fused_attention.py’s synchronous Graph construction. ↗ __init__.py:367↗ fused_attention.py:41

Compare an existing notebook loop with the no-loop branch. See exactly when E1/W0 are used and when the caller waits.

Notebook · event loop already running · all steps
  1. Synchronous realization inside L0

    A lazy tensor’s _sync_realize calls F._run(self.realize). _run detects an already-running event loop, such as a notebook loop.

    ↗ tensor.py:1726↗ __init__.py:373
  2. Avoid nesting a second loop on this thread

    asyncio.run refuses to run inside an existing loop on the same thread. Running a new loop there also fails its _check_running guard. The new loop must be driven elsewhere for this synchronous bridge.

    ↗ runners.py:192↗ base_events.py:635
  3. Create E1 and submit L1’s runner

    MAX creates a new event loop and a short-lived MLIRThreadPoolExecutor, then submits loop.run_until_complete(coro). The coroutine object is an argument passed by reference.

    ↗ __init__.py:376↗ __init__.py:378
  4. Worker enters MLCTX0, then runs L1

    The wrapper enters the default MLIR context on W0. loop.run_until_complete drives the coroutine there, so context-dependent MLIR calls have a current context.

    ↗ _mlir_context.py:49↗ __init__.py:378
  5. Realization returns R1

    L1 drives realization until it completes. The returned object becomes the function result; this does not imply the notebook’s own loop was kept responsive.

    ↗ tensor.py:1720↗ __init__.py:378
  6. Pop scope and finish F1

    W0 exits the MLIR scope; _WorkItem publishes R1. Leaving the executor with-block calls shutdown(wait=True) and joins its worker.

    ↗ _mlir_context.py:50↗ _base.py:647↗ thread.py:31
  7. Return to the notebook call

    _run returns fut.result(). The outer synchronous API can now return, allowing the notebook loop to resume. This executor was scoped to this one _run invocation.

    ↗ __init__.py:379
Ordinary call · no running loop · all steps
  1. No loop is already running

    _in_running_loop catches RuntimeError from get_running_loop and returns False.

    ↗ __init__.py:358
  2. Drive coroutine directly

    _run returns asyncio.run(coro) on this calling thread. It does not construct E1 or submit a worker job in this branch.

    ↗ __init__.py:374
  3. Return the coroutine result

    The coroutine completes and asyncio.run returns the result to _run. MLIR-scoping helpers used by the surrounding API remain separate from this branching decision.

    ↗ __init__.py:374

Concrete objects

L0 = notebook’s running event loop on main; L1 = new loop created by _run; E1 = short-lived executor; W0 = its worker; coro = self.realize coroutine; F1 = Future returned by submit; R1 = realized Tensor. These labels are illustrative identities for the source objects. ↗ __init__.py:376↗ __init__.py:378↗ tensor.py:1720

What happens if we remove the worker?

The tempting asyncio.run(coro) call on the notebook thread raises because L0 is already running. Making a new loop and driving it on that same thread also encounters the running-loop check. MAX drives L1 on W0 and preserves the synchronous return contract. ↗ runners.py:192↗ base_events.py:635

Is this asynchronous for the caller?

The work runs on another thread, but this API is synchronous: exiting the with-block waits for the worker; then fut.result returns. The design does not promise that the notebook’s event loop remains responsive during that wait. ↗ __init__.py:377↗ _base.py:647

Two independent requirements

The separate worker gives L1 a thread without L0’s running-loop conflict. The MLIR wrapper gives W0 an active context for MLIR calls during realization. A plain pool solves the first problem but does not provide the second behavior. ↗ __init__.py:378↗ _mlir_context.py:97

Why not use a pool unconditionally?

When no loop runs, the direct asyncio.run branch already satisfies the synchronous contract. The source creates the pool only for the conflicting case. This helper constructs a fresh executor per such call; it does not reuse a process-wide pool across notebook calls. ↗ __init__.py:367

A second real use: cache a Future for each model specialization

The PyTorch integration schedules session.load(G1). It creates G1 on the caller before submission, and same-signature callers share the cached Future. ↗ torch.py:485↗ torch.py:487

Watch G1 stay a host object, load(G1) enter E1’s queue, and model_cache[K1] retain F1 and then M1.

Two concurrent callers, same key

A acquires the lock, builds G1, stores F1 and releases the lock. B then acquires the lock and sees F1. Both call F1.result outside the lock. Only one load was scheduled for that key, even if neither caller has M1 yet. This is an illustrative interleaving permitted by the actual locking code. ↗ torch.py:474↗ torch.py:487↗ torch.py:490

Two different shapes

K1 can describe float32[32,32] on cuda:0; K2 can describe float32[64,32] on cuda:0. The exact string includes every output/input tensor in order. Different keys create separate cache entries and can submit separate loads, subject to executor capacity and native scheduling. This page claims no measured parallel compilation speedup. ↗ torch.py:469↗ torch.py:457

Does fused_attention.py use this?

No. Its explicit route is Graph → InferenceSession → compile → init → execute. The Torch adapter is a concrete separate caller demonstrating why the reusable executor helper exists. ↗ fused_attention.py:74↗ fused_attention.py:75

Why retain the Future before compilation finishes?

The Future represents in-flight work as well as a finished result. Keeping it in the cache prevents duplicate loads for the same signature. It also delivers the same success or failure to all callers waiting on that entry. ↗ torch.py:487↗ torch.py:490

Why release the lock before waiting?

Only lookup, graph creation and scheduling are serialized by this lock. The result wait is outside it, allowing other callers to find their key or schedule another signature while loading continues. The calling API still waits for its own model. ↗ torch.py:474↗ torch.py:490

Why keep the executor around?

It is captured alongside the cache for this custom-op definition. Later signatures can reuse idle workers. That differs from the notebook helper’s executor, which is constructed and shut down during a single _run call. ↗ torch.py:457↗ __init__.py:377↗ thread.py:186

Which “context” and which “worker”?

TermRole and boundary
MLIR context objectHost-side IR infrastructure: dialects and uniqued types/attributes. A context is not a worker thread. ↗ MLIRContext.h:43
Python MLIR current stackA native thread_local stack used by the Python bindings; context, location and insertion-point scopes are tracked here. ↗ IRCore.cpp:587
MLIRThreadPoolExecutorPython executor; schedules Python callables after wrapping them with default-context scope. Its workers live in this Python process. ↗ _mlir_context.py:89
Native compiler thread poolA separate native MLIR facility. MAX’s MContextExtension can install an AsyncRT::LLVMThreadPool adapter using CPUDevice, subject to the source guards. This is not Python executor.submit. ↗ Context.cpp:44↗ Context.cpp:54
AsyncRT runtime workersExecute native work-queue tasks. Native compiler work can use an adapter to this runtime; that does not make Python executor workers identical to AsyncRT workers. ↗ ThreadPoolWorkQueue.cpp:873
GPU device / CUDA contextLater execution domain and device state. Graph’s Python context guard does not launch a GPU kernel; fused_attention.py calls model.execute separately. ↗ fused_attention.py:82

Continue into native AsyncRT tasks, waits and completion ↗

Inside mlir.Context()

Complete copied answer from src/attention_mlir_context_constructor.md.

_DEFAULT_MLIR_CONTEXT = mlir.Context() creates a Python object backed by a native C++ mlir::MLIRContext, then stores the Python reference in a module-global variable. The native context provides the shared types, attributes, dialect definitions, and diagnostic machinery used when MAX constructs graph IR. See the assignment.

1. First, what does from max import mlir import?

max.mlir exposes MLIR’s Python bindings, including Context. Importing it also registers MAX’s dialects with the Python binding’s shared dialect registry:

from max import mlir
└─ max/mlir/__init__.py
   ├─ expose Context from the MLIR binding
   └─ site_initialize()
      └─ graph.load_modular_dialects(get_dialect_registry())
         └─ M::MO::loadDialects(registry)
            ├─ register MO, MOSH, MAP, MOGG, MGP, …
            └─ register KGEN dialects and translation support

Registration supplies the implementations that understand operations such as mo.graph and mo.custom. The actual graph operations are created later.

Sources: Python import and initialization, native registration, dialect list.

2. The constructor crosses Python → native binding → C API → C++.

There are two constructor layers: a Python Context subclass that performs initialization, and its native base class.

_DEFAULT_MLIR_CONTEXT = mlir.Context()
│
└─ Python Context.__init__()
   │
   ├─ super().__init__()
   │  └─ nanobind invokes the native Context constructor
   │     ├─ mlirContextCreateWithThreading(false)
   │     │  └─ new mlir::MLIRContext(Threading::DISABLED)
   │     │     ├─ allocate MLIRContextImpl
   │     │     ├─ initialize internal registries and storage managers
   │     │     ├─ load the builtin dialect
   │     │     └─ create/cache common types and attributes
   │     │
   │     └─ construct PyMlirContext around the returned handle
   │        └─ record native-context pointer → Python wrapper
   │
   ├─ append_dialect_registry(get_dialect_registry())
   │  └─ attach the registry containing MAX’s dialect registrations
   │
   ├─ apply configured initialization hooks
   │
   ├─ apply the threading policy
   │  └─ MAX’s site initializer suppresses the default LLVM pool
   │
   └─ load_all_available_dialects()
      └─ instantiate the registered dialects for this context
│
└─ assign the returned Python reference to _DEFAULT_MLIR_CONTEXT

This is the default constructor route configured by the files in this checkout.

Sources: Python constructor, nanobind constructor, C API allocation, native initialization.

3. What objects exist in memory afterward?

The ownership/reference picture is approximately:

Python module: max._mlir_context
└─ _DEFAULT_MLIR_CONTEXT
   └─ Python Context object + native PyMlirContext wrapper
      └─ MlirContext handle
         └─ ptr → native mlir::MLIRContext
                  └─ impl → MLIRContextImpl

MlirContext is a small C-compatible handle containing a pointer. It lets the binding refer to the C++ object through the MLIR C API. PyMlirContext retains this handle and maintains a mapping between native context pointers and their Python wrappers. See the handle definition and wrapper implementation.

The substantial compiler state lives in MLIRContextImpl:

Internal storageExampleWhy it exists
loadedDialects, dialectsRegistryBuiltin, MO, MAP, KGENFind the implementation of a dialect and its operations.
Registered operation informationDefinition of mo.graphMake operation metadata and behavior available.
typeUniquer, cached typesf32Ty, int64TyReuse representations of identical types.
attributeUniquer, cached attributesStrings, unknown location, empty dictionaryReuse common immutable metadata.
affineUniquerAffine expressions and mapsShare representations used for indexing and shape calculations.
diagEngineErrors and attached locationsReport problems encountered while processing IR.
threadPoolInitially unset on this construction routeProvide a compiler work scheduler when subsequently configured.

These are actual fields in MLIRContextImpl. Its operation registry describes operations; your particular GraphOp and its body are created separately.

4. Example: why shared type storage helps

Consider these illustrative calls:

with _DEFAULT_MLIR_CONTEXT:
    a = mlir.IntegerType.get_signless(64)
    b = mlir.IntegerType.get_signless(64)

Both requests use the same native context:

request a: signless i64 ──┐
                         ├──→ context’s cached int64Ty
request b: signless i64 ──┘

The context already initialized this common type. IntegerType::get() checks the cache and returns the existing native type representation. Thus many tensor types or operations can refer to the same i64 type storage. This concerns native type identity; it does not require the Python wrapper objects to satisfy a is b. See IntegerType::get().

5. Creating the object and making it “current” are separate steps.

Immediately after construction, MAX executes:

_DEFAULT_MLIR_CONTEXT.__enter__()

That follows this path:

_DEFAULT_MLIR_CONTEXT.__enter__()
└─ PyMlirContext::contextEnter(context)
   └─ PyThreadContextEntry::pushContext(context)
      └─ push a reference onto this thread’s context stack

mlir.Context.current
└─ read the context from this thread’s top stack entry

The stack is declared thread_local. Therefore, two threads can reference the same context object while each maintains its own current-context selection. Entering it on the importing thread does not automatically enter it on another thread. Sources: MAX’s explicit enter, thread-local stack and lookup.

6. Where does AsyncRT enter this picture?

In this checkout, _site_initialize_0.py sets:

disable_multithreading = True

This suppresses creation of a separate default LLVM pool for every Python context. MAX subsequently connects compiler scheduling to its runtime through this route:

KernelLibrary.__init__()
└─ _init_and_register_max_context(context)
   └─ M::registerContext(mlirContext, maxContext)
      └─ MContextExtension::apply(...)
         ├─ obtain/create AsyncRT::LLVMThreadPool using CPUDevice
         └─ mlirContext.setThreadPool(pool)
QnA 6.1 · mlirContext.setThreadPool(pool) — why do we need a thread pool here? Why MLIRThreadPoolExecutor?

They serve two different purposes: setThreadPool(pool) gives native MLIR compiler work a scheduler; MLIRThreadPoolExecutor runs Python functions on workers while ensuring those workers have an active MLIR context.

mlirContext.setThreadPool(pool)MLIRThreadPoolExecutor
LayerNative C++ compilerPython orchestration
Work submittedCompiler tasks: analyses, transformations, independent functionsPython callables, such as session.load(graph)
WorkersIn MAX, supplied through AsyncRT’s CPU work queuePython ThreadPoolExecutor workers
Main purposeEnable compiler parallelism and reuse runtime workersRun background Python work with the correct current MLIR context

Sources: native pool adapter, Python executor implementation.

For mlirContext.setThreadPool(pool), the reason is compiler parallelism and control over worker resources.

An MLIR context can operate with multithreading disabled. Installing a pool enables eligible compiler work to run concurrently. MLIR can share an externally supplied pool across contexts; that pool must outlive the contexts using it. (mlir.llvm.org)

In your checkout, its implementation is essentially:

void MLIRContext::setThreadPool(llvm::ThreadPoolInterface &pool) {
    // Requires multithreading to be disabled beforehand.
    impl->threadPool = &pool;
    impl->ownedThreadPool.reset();
    enableMultithreading();
}

This attaches a scheduler. Actual tasks are submitted later, when compiler code requests parallel execution. See the implementation.

MAX explicitly disables MLIR’s initial default pool. Its source explains why: otherwise every Python MLIR context receives its own LLVM pool, whose default sizing ignores cgroup CPU quotas. MAX instead connects the context to AsyncRT’s CPU work queue. See MAX’s threading policy.

The setup path is:

KernelLibrary.__init__()
└─ _init_and_register_max_context(mlir_context)
   ├─ obtain/create the MAX context containing an AsyncRT CPUDevice
   └─ M::registerContext(...)
      └─ MContextExtension::apply(...)
         ├─ obtain/create AsyncRT::LLVMThreadPool(cpuDevice)
         └─ context->setThreadPool(*tp)

The final installation is conditional: MAX checks whether MLIR already has multithreading enabled, whether pool attachment is permitted, and whether a suitable CPUDevice/pool exists.

Sources: KernelLibrary caller, native registration, pool attachment.

A concrete example of work that uses this pool: MAX’s AnonymizeDimNamesPass processes independent MOGG functions through mlir::parallelForEach.

AnonymizeDimNamesPass::runOnOperation()
└─ collect MOGG functions
   └─ mlir::parallelForEach(context, functions, stripStubDimNames)
      ├─ get the context's installed thread pool
      ├─ submit compiler tasks through ThreadPoolTaskGroup
      │  └─ AsyncRT::LLVMThreadPool::asyncEnqueue(...)
      │     └─ CPUDevice.workQueue.addTask(...)
      │        └─ CPU worker executes the compiler function
      └─ wait for this task group to finish

Sources: actual compiler pass, MLIR parallel scheduling, AsyncRT task submission.

For illustration, with three independent functions and available workers:

Sequential:  caller → process fA → process fB → process fC

Concurrent:  worker W0 → process fA
             worker W1 → process fB
             worker W2 → process fC
             caller waits for completion

MLIR supports parallel processing of independent operations. Dependent compiler stages still preserve their required ordering. (mlir.llvm.org)

For MLIRThreadPoolExecutor, the reason is background Python execution plus per-thread context setup.

Python’s ordinary ThreadPoolExecutor schedules a callable and returns a Future, representing its eventual result. (docs.python.org) MAX adds a small wrapper:

class MLIRThreadPoolExecutor(ThreadPoolExecutor):
    def submit(self, fn, /, *args, **kwargs):
        return super().submit(
            call_with_default_mlir_context, fn, *args, **kwargs
        )

The wrapper executes on the worker thread:

Caller submits fn
└─ Python worker picks up the task
   └─ call_with_default_mlir_context(fn, ...)
      ├─ inspect mlir.Context.current on this worker
      ├─ if absent: enter _DEFAULT_MLIR_CONTEXT
      ├─ run fn(...)
      └─ exit the temporary context scope

If a context is already active on that worker, the helper preserves it. See the wrapper implementation.

Why is entering the context necessary? The default context object is shared, but “current context” is selected separately for each thread. Entering it on the main thread does not automatically enter it on a newly created worker:

Shared object: _DEFAULT_MLIR_CONTEXT = Ctx1

Main thread:
    Context.current → Ctx1

New Python worker, before wrapper:
    Context.current → None

Same worker, inside wrapper:
    Context.current → Ctx1

MAX documents this distinction directly in its context helpers.

There are two concrete callers in this repository:

  • Notebook support: when an asyncio loop is already running, MAX’s _run() helper executes the coroutine using another thread and another event loop. The executor ensures MLIR APIs used there have a current context. See the notebook-compatible helper.
  • PyTorch custom operations: MAX submits self.library._session.load(graph) to this executor and caches its future by tensor signature. Callers requesting the same signature reuse that future. See the actual submission and cache.

For your fused-attention example, a Python pool is not required just to construct G1. The example builds the graph directly on its caller thread, and Graph.__init__ already has @in_default_mlir_context. Native compilation can subsequently use the installed AsyncRT-backed compiler pool.

Sources: fused-attention graph construction, Graph constructor decorator.

That installation is conditional: the extension checks whether threading is already enabled and whether a suitable runtime pool is available. This native compiler pool is also distinct from MLIRThreadPoolExecutor, whose Python job is to run submitted functions with an appropriate current MLIR context.

Sources: MAX’s initial threading policy, KernelLibrary registration, AsyncRT pool attachment, Python executor.

from __future__ import annotations

import atexit
import contextlib
import functools
import inspect
from collections.abc import Callable, Generator
from concurrent.futures import Future, ThreadPoolExecutor
from typing import ParamSpec, TypeVar

from max import mlir

_DEFAULT_MLIR_CONTEXT = mlir.Context()
# MLIR Context.current is thread-local.
# - Keep the global context entered for the main thread.
# - Run worker tasks via helpers/executors in this module so MLIR APIs run
#   with a scoped context (avoids nanobind GIL/TLS teardown crashes).
# - atexit handler ensures the context is exited on shutdown.
_DEFAULT_MLIR_CONTEXT.__enter__()
atexit.register(_DEFAULT_MLIR_CONTEXT.__exit__, None, None, None)

P = ParamSpec("P")
R = TypeVar("R")


def default_mlir_context() -> mlir.Context:
    """Returns the global MLIR context."""
    return _DEFAULT_MLIR_CONTEXT


def call_with_default_mlir_context(
    fn: Callable[P, R], /, *args: P.args, **kwargs: P.kwargs
) -> R:
    context = mlir.Context.current
    if context is None:
        with _DEFAULT_MLIR_CONTEXT:
            return fn(*args, **kwargs)
    return fn(*args, **kwargs)


@contextlib.contextmanager
def ensure_default_mlir_context() -> Generator[None]:
    """Ensure the default MLIR context is entered for the current thread.

    Sister to :func:`call_with_default_mlir_context` for use as a context
    manager. ``mlir.Context.current`` is thread-local; background threads
    do not automatically have the default context entered. This enters it
    only if no context is already active.
    """
    if mlir.Context.current is None:
        with _DEFAULT_MLIR_CONTEXT:
            yield
    else:
        yield


def in_default_mlir_context(fn: Callable[P, R]) -> Callable[P, R]:
    """Decorator equivalent of ``with ensure_default_mlir_context():``. Sync + async."""
    if inspect.iscoroutinefunction(fn):

        @functools.wraps(fn)
        async def async_wrapper(*args: P.args, **kwargs: P.kwargs) -> R:
            with ensure_default_mlir_context():
                return await fn(*args, **kwargs)

        return async_wrapper  # type: ignore[return-value]

    @functools.wraps(fn)
    def wrapper(*args: P.args, **kwargs: P.kwargs) -> R:
        with ensure_default_mlir_context():
            return fn(*args, **kwargs)

    return wrapper


class MLIRThreadPoolExecutor(ThreadPoolExecutor):
    def submit(
        self,
        fn: Callable[P, R],
        /,
        *args: P.args,
        **kwargs: P.kwargs,
    ) -> Future[R]:
        return super().submit(
            call_with_default_mlir_context, fn, *args, **kwargs
        )

"""MLIR bindings used by :mod:`max.graph`, plus Modular dialect registration.

Re-exports the MLIR Python binding objects (``Context``, ``Operation``,
``Module``, and friends). :func:`site_initialize` registers MAX's custom
dialects with MLIR and runs when the module is imported.
"""

from .._mlir._mlir_libs._mlir.ir import (
    ArrayAttr,
    Attribute,
    Block,
    BoolAttr,
    Context,
    Diagnostic,
    DictAttr,
    FunctionType,
    IndexType,
    InsertionPoint,
    IntegerAttr,
    Location,
    MLIRError,
    Module,
    Operation,
    OpView,
    StringAttr,
    Type,
    TypeAttr,
    Value,
)


def site_initialize() -> None:
    """Registers MAX's custom MLIR dialects with the global registry.

    Runs automatically when :mod:`max.mlir` is imported.
    """
    from max._core import graph  # type: ignore[import-not-found]

    # This ignore is needed externally but not internally
    from .._mlir._mlir_libs import (  # type: ignore[attr-defined, unused-ignore]
        get_dialect_registry,
    )

    graph.load_modular_dialects(get_dialect_registry())


site_initialize()

// Backs Graph profile scope's _location() wrap loop: wraps `child` in a
// MOGG::ProfileScopeLocationAttr naming the active scope.
MlirLocation profile_scope_location(MlirContext ctx, const std::string &name,
                                    MlirLocation child,
                                    std::optional<std::string> color);

namespace nb = nanobind;
using namespace M::Graph;

// For named argument shorthand.
// See:
// https://nanobind.readthedocs.io/en/stable/basics.html#keyword-and-default-arguments
using namespace nanobind::literals;

namespace {
void load_modular_dialects(MlirDialectRegistry registry) {
  M::MO::loadDialects(*unwrap(registry));
}

MlirOperation next_operation(MlirOperation op) {
  mlir::Operation *x = unwrap(op);
  return wrap(x->getNextNode());
}

MlirOperation prev_operation(MlirOperation op) {
  mlir::Operation *x = unwrap(op);
  return wrap(x->getPrevNode());
}

MlirOperation last_operation(MlirBlock block) {
  mlir::Block *x = unwrap(block);

  if (x->empty())
    return wrap((mlir::Operation *)nullptr);
  return wrap(&x->back());
}

/// Initializes M::Context when no global context exists, then registers it on
/// the given MLIR context so loadContext() succeeds for graph compilation and
/// kernel analysis.
///
/// Reuses the existing global M::Context when present (e.g. after
/// InferenceSession) if Init::Options match; otherwise creates it via
/// Init::getOrCreateContext with cpuDevice options aligned with
/// Engine::Context::create's default session (see comments in-body).
static void _init_and_register_max_context(MlirContext mlirCtx) {
  M::Init::Options options;
  M::AsyncRT::CPUDeviceOptions rtOptions;
  // AsyncRT::CPUDeviceOptions defaults mainWillDonate to true; Engine's
  // getOrCreateCPUDeviceOptions forces false.
  rtOptions.mainWillDonate = false;
  options.withCPUDeviceOptions(rtOptions);
  // Engine::Config defaults isCrashLogEnabled() to false;
  // Engine::Context::create passes withForceDisableCrashReporting(!that).
  options.withForceDisableCrashReporting(true);

  auto ctxOr = M::Init::getOrCreateContext("max-graph", options);
  if (ctxOr.isError())
    throw std::runtime_error(ctxOr.takeError().get());
  M::ContextRef maxContext = ctxOr.takeValue();

  M::registerContext(*unwrap(mlirCtx), maxContext);
}

M::ArrayElementsAttr array_attr(M::Driver::Python::Buffer &buffer,
                                M::MO::TensorType &type) {
  // Create an ND array from data, taking the size and shape from the tensor
  // type argument.
  auto spec = buffer.getSpec();

  llvm::ArrayRef<uint8_t> bytesArray(llvm::bit_cast<uint8_t *>(buffer.data()),
                                     spec.getSizeInBytes());

  auto dims = llvm::SmallVector<int64_t>(spec.begin(), spec.end());
  auto shapedType =
      mlir::RankedTensorType::get(type.getIntDims(), type.getElementType());

  return M::ArrayElementsAttr::get({bytesArray.data(), bytesArray.size()},
                                   shapedType);
}

char *frame_traceback(void *frame_ptr) {
  // This is simply
  // `''.join(traceback.format_list(frame))`
  nb::gil_scoped_acquire acquire{};
  auto frame = nb::handle(reinterpret_cast<PyObject *>(frame_ptr));
  nb::object os = nb::module_::import_("traceback");
  nb::object formatStack = os.attr("format_list");
  auto empty = nb::str("");
  nb::object emptyJoin = empty.attr("join");

  auto outStr = nb::cast<std::string>(emptyJoin(formatStack(frame)));

  char *out = new char[outStr.size() + 1]{};
  // Copy to a string owned by the caller.
  outStr.copy(out, outStr.size());
  return out;
}

void frame_decref(void *frame_ptr) {
  // Destruction is always on the main thread controlled by python.
  // It will always have the gil.
  auto frame = nb::handle(reinterpret_cast<PyObject *>(frame_ptr));
  frame.dec_ref();
}

void frame_incref(void *frame_ptr) {
  // Destruction is always on the main thread controlled by python.
  // It will always have the gil.
  auto frame = nb::handle(reinterpret_cast<PyObject *>(frame_ptr));
  frame.inc_ref();
}

MlirLocation frame_loc(MlirContext ctx, nb::handle frame) {
  // The resulting location handles incrementing and decrementing the object's
  // reference count, as the object will be interned on the MLIR context.
  mlir::Location loc = M::RMO::PythonFrameAttr::getOpaque(
      unwrap(ctx), {.ptr = frame.ptr(),
                    .to_str = &frame_traceback,
                    .incref = &frame_incref,
                    .decref = &frame_decref});
  return wrap(loc);
}

// Serializes op and its descendants to MLIR bytecode with each op's
// Python-frame source location spelled out. The frames are attached as
// OpaqueLocs that hold a live callback and do not survive serialization, so
// they are materialized into serializable FusedLocs first. The materialization
// runs on a clone, so the caller's operation keeps its live OpaqueLocs.
//
// Bytecode rather than assembly text because this extension static-links its
// own LLVM: its textual float printer matches APFloat semantics by pointer
// against its own copy of the APFloatBase::sem* statics, so it mangles f64
// constants and aborts on any f32 that MLIR spells as a hex literal. Callers
// reparse this through max.mlir, which shares libmax's copy, and print there.
// See GEX-4052.
nb::bytes source_locations_bytecode(mlir::OpState &op) {
  mlir::OwningOpRef<mlir::Operation *> clone(op.getOperation()->clone());
  M::RMO::materializePythonFrameLocations(clone.get());
  std::string result;
  llvm::raw_string_ostream os(result);
  if (mlir::failed(mlir::writeBytecodeToFile(clone.get(), os)))
    throw std::runtime_error(
        "Failed to serialize operation with source locations to bytecode");
  return nb::bytes(result.data(), result.size());
}

/// Creates a Buffer directly from an MLIR constant attribute.
///
/// Supports:
/// - ArrayElementsAttr (#M.dense_array)
/// - AlignedBytesAttr (#M.aligned_bytes)
/// - DenseResourceElementsAttr (external blob)
///
/// Always copies data into a new buffer. Handles splatting when source
/// has 1 element but target shape requires more.
M::Driver::Python::Buffer
buffer_from_constant_attr(mlir::ElementsAttr attr, M::DType dtype,
                          const std::vector<size_t> &shape,
                          M::Driver::Python::PyDeviceTy device) {
  // Extract raw bytes based on attribute type
  llvm::ArrayRef<uint8_t> rawData;

  if (auto arrayAttr = llvm::dyn_cast<M::ArrayElementsAttr>(attr)) {
    rawData = arrayAttr.getRawData();
  } else if (auto alignedAttr = llvm::dyn_cast<M::AlignedBytesAttr>(attr)) {
    rawData = alignedAttr.getData();
  } else if (auto denseResource =
                 llvm::dyn_cast<mlir::DenseResourceElementsAttr>(attr)) {
    auto blob = denseResource.getRawHandle().getBlob();
    if (!blob)
      throw std::runtime_error("DenseResourceElementsAttr has no blob data");
    auto blobData = blob->getData();
    rawData = llvm::ArrayRef<uint8_t>(
        reinterpret_cast<const uint8_t *>(blobData.data()), blobData.size());
  } else {
    throw std::runtime_error(
        "Unsupported constant attribute type for buffer creation");
  }

  // Calculate element counts
  size_t targetNumElements = 1;
  for (size_t dim : shape)
    targetNumElements *= dim;

  size_t elementSize = dtype.getSizeInBytes();
  size_t srcNumElements = rawData.size() / elementSize;

  // Validate for splatting
  if (srcNumElements != targetNumElements && srcNumElements != 1) {
    throw std::runtime_error(
        "Invalid constant: source has " + std::to_string(srcNumElements) +
        " elements but target has " + std::to_string(targetNumElements) +
        " elements (not a splat)");
  }

  // TODO(MXF-106): use Buffer.frombuffer when available.
  // Create buffer and copy data
  M::Driver::Python::Buffer buffer(dtype, shape, device);
  uint8_t *dstData = static_cast<uint8_t *>(buffer.data());

  if (srcNumElements == targetNumElements) {
    // Direct copy
    std::memcpy(dstData, rawData.data(), rawData.size());
  } else {
    // Splat: replicate single element
    for (size_t i = 0; i < targetNumElements; ++i) {
      std::memcpy(dstData + i * elementSize, rawData.data(), elementSize);
    }
  }

  return buffer;
}

} // namespace

void M::Graph::Python::bindGraphModule(nb::module_ m) {
  m.doc() = R"nbdoc(
        Provides Python bindings for the MAX Graph API.
    )nbdoc";

  /// Attribute factories

  /// Register dialects needed to build MAX graphs.
  m.def("load_modular_dialects", &load_modular_dialects,
        "Registers all Modular MLIR dialects into the given registry.");

  /// Creates an array attribute from any Python object that implements the
  /// buffer protocol.
  /// Copies the buffer data into the array attribute interned into the
  /// MLIRContext.
  m.def("array_attr", &array_attr,
        "Creates an array attribute from a buffer and tensor type.");

  /// Creates a Buffer from an MLIR constant attribute (inverse of array_attr).
  /// Copies data and handles splatting.
  m.def("_buffer_from_constant_attr", &buffer_from_constant_attr,
        nb::arg("attr"), nb::arg("dtype"), nb::arg("shape"), nb::arg("device"),
        "Creates a Buffer from an MLIR constant attribute.");

  m.def("next_operation", &next_operation,
        "Returns the next operation in the parent block, or ``None``.");
  m.def("prev_operation", &prev_operation,
        "Returns the previous operation in the parent block, or ``None``.");
  m.def("last_operation", &last_operation,
        "Returns the last operation in the given block, or ``None``.");

  /// Converts a dtype to an MLIR type.
  m.def("dtype_to_type",
        infer_context(+[](mlir::MLIRContext *ctx, M::DType dtype) {
          auto mlirType = M::MO::toMLIRType(ctx, dtype);
          if (mlirType.isError())
            throw std::runtime_error("Invalid dtype");
          return *mlirType;
        }),
        "Converts a MAX :class:`DType` to the corresponding MLIR type.");

  m.def(
      "type_to_dtype",
      [](mlir::Type dtype) -> M::DType {
        ErrorOr<DType> type = M::MO::fromMLIRType(dtype);
        if (type.isError())
          throw std::runtime_error("Invalid type");
        return *type;
      },
      "Converts an MLIR type to the corresponding MAX :class:`DType`.");

  /// Creates an opaque location containing a python frame.
  m.def("frame_loc", &frame_loc,
        "Creates an opaque MLIR location containing a Python stack frame.");

  m.def("profile_scope_location", &profile_scope_location, "ctx"_a, "name"_a,
        "child"_a, "color"_a = std::nullopt,
        "Wraps `child` in a MOGG::ProfileScopeLocationAttr naming the active "
        "Graph.profile_scope(), with an optional color.");

  /// Serializes an operation to MLIR bytecode with Python source locations
  /// materialized, so a graph dumped without compiling it still shows where
  /// each op was built. Does not mutate the operation.
  m.def("source_locations_bytecode", &source_locations_bytecode, "op"_a,
        "Serializes the operation to MLIR bytecode with each op's Python "
        "source location materialized into printable form. Print it by "
        "reparsing through max.mlir. Does not mutate the operation.");

  m.def("_init_and_register_max_context", &_init_and_register_max_context,
        "mlir_ctx"_a,
        R"nbdoc(
      Initializes a process-wide M::Context when none exists, then registers it with the given MLIR context so compiler code can use loadContext.

      Internal API; does not expose M::Context to Python. New contexts are
      created via Init::getOrCreateContext (same Init path the Engine uses before
      attaching devices).
  )nbdoc");

  //===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
  // KernelLibrary (backed by `mogg.kernel.decl` / `mogg.primitive.decl` ops)
  //===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

  nb::class_<Python::KernelTorchInfo>(m, "KernelTorchInfo", R"nbdoc(
      The info needed to register a Mojo kernel as a PyTorch custom op.

      Built by :obj:`max.experimental.torch` from the kernel's ``execute``
      signature via ``KernelDeclAdaptor``.
  )nbdoc")
      .def_ro("num_dps_outputs", &Python::KernelTorchInfo::numDpsOutputs,
              "The number of leading destination-passing-style output "
              "arguments.")
      .def_ro("tensor_arg_names", &Python::KernelTorchInfo::tensorArgNames,
              "The source names of tensor-like arguments in declaration "
              "order (DPS outputs first, then inputs).");

  nb::class_<Python::Analysis>(m, "Analysis", R"nbdoc(
      Analyzes Mojo kernel libraries for custom operator integration.

      Loads one or more Mojo shared libraries and exposes their exported
      kernel operations for use in MAX graphs. Used internally to validate
      and register custom operations.

      Args:
          context: A Mojo library object or path.
          paths: The additional library search paths.
  )nbdoc")
      .def(nb::init<nb::object, std::vector<std::filesystem::path>>(),
           "context"_a, "paths"_a)
      .def_prop_ro("symbol_names", &Analysis::symbolNames,
                   "The list of exported kernel symbol names.")
      .def_prop_ro("library_paths", &Analysis::libraryPaths,
                   "The paths of all loaded libraries.")
      .def(
          "kernel",
          [](Analysis *self, const std::string &name) {
            return M::Graph::Python::castOp(self->kernelOp(name));
          },
          "Returns the MLIR operation for the named kernel symbol.")
      .def("verify_custom_op", &Analysis::verifyCustomOp,
           "Verifies that an operation matches the expected kernel signature.")
      .def("add_path", &Analysis::addPath,
           "Adds a library search path to this analysis.")
      .def("seed_kernel_decls", &Analysis::seedKernelDecls,
           "Copies kernel decl ops and the opaque-type mapping attribute "
           "into the given target module. Called by the compile path to "
           "seed a model module so the GC pipeline can skip "
           "``mogg-import-packages``.")
      .def("kernel_torch_info", &Analysis::kernelTorchInfo, "name"_a,
           "Returns the :class:`KernelTorchInfo` that "
           ":obj:`max.experimental.torch` needs to register the named kernel "
           "as a PyTorch custom op. Raises ``ValueError`` if the kernel is "
           "unknown or has an unsupported argument type.")
      .def("has_shape_function", &Analysis::hasShapeFunction, "name"_a,
           "Returns true if a shape function is registered for the named "
           "kernel.");

  M::Profiler::Python::addTracingToNanobindModuleClassMethods(
      m, "max._core.graph.");
}

MlirLocation profile_scope_location(MlirContext ctx, const std::string &name,
                                    MlirLocation child,
                                    std::optional<std::string> color) {
  mlir::MLIRContext *ctxPtr = unwrap(ctx);
  mlir::StringAttr colorAttr =
      color ? mlir::StringAttr::get(ctxPtr, *color) : mlir::StringAttr();
  mlir::Location loc = M::MOGG::ProfileScopeLocationAttr::get(
      ctxPtr, mlir::StringAttr::get(ctxPtr, name), unwrap(child), colorAttr);
  return wrap(loc);
}

void M::MO::loadDialects(mlir::DialectRegistry &registry) {
  registry.insert<MO::MODialect, MOSH::MOSHDialect, MOGG::MOGGDialect,
                  MGP::MGPDialect, GRT::GRTDialect, RMO::RMODialect,
                  MAP::MAPDialect>();
  M::registerAllKGENDialects(registry);
  M::registerKGENToLLVMTranslation(registry);
}

void M::MO::registerShapeInferencePipeline() {
  mlir::PassPipelineRegistration<>(
      "mo-shape-inference", "Run the end-to-end shape inference pipeline.",
      buildShapeInferencePipeline);
}

void M::MO::buildJitPipeline(mlir::OpPassManager &pm) {
  pm.addPass(MOGG::createLowerCompiledRoutines());
  pm.addPass(MGP::createInlineMGPCallsPass());
  pm.addPass(MGP::createFixupOverhangsPass());
  pm.addPass(mlir::createCSEPass());
  pm.addPass(MGP::createSimplifyChainsPass());
  pm.addPass(mlir::createCanonicalizerPass());
  pm.addPass(mlir::createCSEPass());
  pm.addPass(MGP::createOutlineModelsToCallables());
}

namespace {
static void gcPipelineImpl(mlir::OpPassManager &pm,
                           const GCPipelineOptions &opts, bool skipJit,
                           bool dumpIntermediates = false);
} // namespace

void M::MO::registerGCPipeline() {
  mlir::PassPipelineRegistration<GCPipelineOptions>(
      "gc-pipeline", "Full graph-compiler pipeline (MO → MGP → JIT).",
      [](mlir::OpPassManager &pm, const GCPipelineOptions &opts) {
        // Enable dumps here so buildGCPipeline stays dump-free for cache keys.
        gcPipelineImpl(pm, opts, /*skipJit=*/false,
                       /*dumpIntermediates=*/!getMaxIRDumpDir().empty());
      });
}

void M::MO::registerGCPipelineThroughEmitMojo() {
  mlir::PassPipelineRegistration<GCPipelineOptions>(
      "gc-pipeline-pre-jit",
      "Graph compiler through emit-mojo (MO → MGP → emit-mojo; no JIT).",
      [](mlir::OpPassManager &pm, const GCPipelineOptions &opts) {
        gcPipelineImpl(pm, opts, /*skipJit=*/true,
                       /*dumpIntermediates=*/!getMaxIRDumpDir().empty());
      });
}

void M::MO::registerMoPipeline() {
  mlir::PassPipelineRegistration<MoPipelineOptions>(
      "mo-pipeline",
      "Passes from graph input up to (but not including) mo-to-mogg.",
      [](mlir::OpPassManager &pm, const MoPipelineOptions &opts) {
        buildMoPipeline(pm, opts);
      });
}

void M::MO::registerMapPipeline() {
  mlir::PassPipelineRegistration<MapPipelineOptions>(
      "map-pipeline",
      "Passes between mo-to-map and mogg-to-mgp (both excluded).",
      [](mlir::OpPassManager &pm, const MapPipelineOptions &opts) {
        buildMapPipeline(pm, opts);
      });
}

void M::MO::registerMoggPipeline() {
  mlir::PassPipelineRegistration<MoggPipelineOptions>(
      "mogg-pipeline",
      "Passes between mo-to-mogg and mogg-to-mgp (both excluded).",
      [](mlir::OpPassManager &pm, const MoggPipelineOptions &opts) {
        buildMoggPipeline(pm, opts);
      });
}

void M::MO::registerMgpPipeline() {
  mlir::PassPipelineRegistration<MgpPipelineOptions>(
      "mgp-pipeline", "Passes between mogg-to-mgp and jit (both excluded).",
      [](mlir::OpPassManager &pm, const MgpPipelineOptions &opts) {
        buildMgpPipeline(pm, opts);
      });
}

void M::MO::registerJitPipeline() {
  mlir::PassPipelineRegistration<>(
      "jit-pipeline", "Passes that run after the jit pass.",
      [](mlir::OpPassManager &pm) { buildJitPipeline(pm); });
}

LogicalResult MO::runGcPipeline(ModuleOp module,
                                const GCPipelineOptions &gcPipelineOptions) {

  mlir::PassManager pm = mlir::PassManager::on<ModuleOp>(
      module.getContext(), mlir::OpPassManager::Nesting::Implicit);

  if (!gcPipelineOptions.mlirTimingOutDir.empty()) {
    const char *pipelineName = "GC Pipeline";
    auto enabledTiming = M::configureMLIRPassTimingJSONOutput(
        pm, gcPipelineOptions.mlirTimingOutDir.getValue(), pipelineName);
    if (enabledTiming.isError()) {
      llvm::errs() << enabledTiming.getError() << "\n";
      return failure();
    }
  }

  MO::buildGCPipeline(pm, gcPipelineOptions);
  return pm.run(module);
}

void M::MO::buildMoPipeline(mlir::OpPassManager &pm,
                            const MoPipelineOptions &opts) {
  auto kernelLibraryPaths =
      llvm::to_vector_of<std::string>(opts.kernelLibraryPaths);

  // Skipped when the caller already seeded decls and
  // `mogg.opaque_type_mapping` via `MOGG::copyKernelDecls`. RewriteOpaqueTypes
  // still runs so freshly-cloned `!mo.opaque<"simple">` uses get rewritten.
  if (!opts.kernelDeclsPrePopulated) {
    pm.addPass(MOGG::createImportPackages(
        {.mojoPkgPaths = kernelLibraryPaths, .litMlirPaths = {}}));
    pm.addPass(MOGG::createVerifyKernels());
  }

  pm.addPass(MOGG::createRewriteOpaqueTypes());
  pm.addPass(KGEN::createVerifyParameters());

  if (opts.debugPrintAllTensors)
    pm.addPass(MO::createDebugPrintAllTensorsPass());

  pm.addPass(RMO::createLegalizeRMOOps());

  pm.addNestedPass<GraphOp>(mlir::createCSEPass());
  pm.addNestedPass<GraphOp>(mlir::createCanonicalizerPass());
  pm.addPass(MO::createCanonicalizeChainSequences());

  pm.addNestedPass<GraphOp>(mlir::createCanonicalizerPass());
  pm.addNestedPass<GraphOp>(mlir::createCSEPass());

  std::string_view compiledFrameworkLabel;
  if (opts.compiledFrameworkLabel.hasValue())
    compiledFrameworkLabel = opts.compiledFrameworkLabel;

  std::optional<std::string> cacheDir;
  if (opts.cacheDir.hasValue())
    cacheDir = opts.cacheDir;

  if (opts.useShapeInference)
    buildShapeInferencePipeline(pm);

  // TODO(GEX-886): Remove symbolic optimization's dependency on constant
  // folding.
  if (opts.constantFold)
    pm.addPass(MO::createConstantFoldPass(compiledFrameworkLabel, cacheDir,
                                          kernelLibraryPaths));

  pm.addPass(MO::createHoistConstantSubgraphsIntoParent());
  pm.addNestedPass<MO::GraphOp>(mlir::createCSEPass());

  SymbolicOptimizationOptions symbolicOptimizationOpts;
  symbolicOptimizationOpts.symbolicFfastMath = opts.symbolicFfastMath;
  symbolicOptimizationOpts.symbolicNoUndefinedMath =
      opts.symbolicNoUndefinedMath;

  pm.addPass(MO::createSymbolicOptimization(symbolicOptimizationOpts));
  pm.addNestedPass<GraphOp>(mlir::createCanonicalizerPass());
  pm.addNestedPass<GraphOp>(mlir::createCSEPass());

  pm.addPass(MO::createMergeDuplicateShapeMaterializations());
  pm.addPass(MO::createAddFallbackShapeFunctions());
  pm.addPass(MO::createSymbolicOptimization(symbolicOptimizationOpts));
  pm.addNestedPass<GraphOp>(mlir::createCanonicalizerPass());
  pm.addNestedPass<GraphOp>(mlir::createCSEPass());

  if (opts.constantFold)
    pm.addPass(MO::createConstantFoldPass(compiledFrameworkLabel, cacheDir,
                                          kernelLibraryPaths));

  pm.addPass(MO::createInferLayouts());
  if (opts.usePatterns) {
    MOGG::PatternFusionOptions patternFusionOpts;
    patternFusionOpts.mhaAllowUnsafeBCast =
        opts.patternFusionMHAAllowUnsafeBCasts;
    patternFusionOpts.mhaAllowInternalReshape =
        opts.patternFusionMHAAllowInternalReshape;
    patternFusionOpts.enableMHAPattern = opts.patternFusionMHAEnable;
    patternFusionOpts.targetDevice = opts.defaultDeviceLabel;
    patternFusionOpts.targetDeviceId = opts.defaultDeviceId;
    pm.addPass(MOGG::createPatternFusion(patternFusionOpts));

    InvokeShapePackingFunctionsOptions shapeFuncOptions;
    shapeFuncOptions.sanityCheckShapeFuncs = opts.sanityCheckShapeFuncs;

    pm.addPass(MO::createInvokeShapePackingFunctions(shapeFuncOptions));
    pm.addPass(MO::createPropagateShapes());
    pm.addNestedPass<GraphOp>(mlir::createCanonicalizerPass());
    pm.addNestedPass<GraphOp>(mlir::createCSEPass());
  }

  MO::ValidateDevicesPassOptions validateDevicesPassOpt;
  validateDevicesPassOpt.defaultDeviceTargetTriple =
      opts.defaultDeviceTargetTriple;
  validateDevicesPassOpt.defaultDeviceTargetArch = opts.defaultDeviceTargetArch;
  pm.addPass(MO::createValidateDevicesPass(validateDevicesPassOpt));

  pm.addNestedPass<GraphOp>(mlir::createCanonicalizerPass());
  pm.addNestedPass<GraphOp>(mlir::createCSEPass());

  // Absorb per-device consumers of an mo.tensor.unbundle back into the
  // producing mo.parallel (canonicalize collapses bundle(unbundle(X)) to X) so
  // epilogue fusion sees a single kernel body.
  pm.addPass(MO::createCreateParallelFromUnbundle());
  pm.addNestedPass<GraphOp>(mlir::createCanonicalizerPass());
  pm.addPass(MO::createMergeAdjacentParallels());

  if (opts.constantFold)
    pm.addPass(MO::createConstantFoldPass(compiledFrameworkLabel, cacheDir,
                                          kernelLibraryPaths));

  if (opts.fuseJitKernels) {
    // Without fusion this can add extraneous copies.
    pm.addPass(MO::createElideRedundantMutableOps());
  }

  pm.addPass(MO::createHoistParameterExpressions());
  pm.addNestedPass<GraphOp>(mlir::createCanonicalizerPass());
  pm.addPass(MO::createRemoveUnusedOps());
}

void M::MO::buildMapPipeline(mlir::OpPassManager &pm,
                             const MapPipelineOptions &opts) {
  pm.addNestedPass<GraphOp>(mlir::createCanonicalizerPass());
  pm.addNestedPass<GraphOp>(mlir::createCSEPass());

  pm.addNestedPass<GraphOp>(MAP::createFuseKernels());
  if (opts.fuseMutableLoadStore)
    pm.addNestedPass<GraphOp>(MAP::createFuseMutableLoads());
  pm.addNestedPass<GraphOp>(mlir::createCanonicalizerPass());
  pm.addNestedPass<GraphOp>(mlir::createCSEPass());

  // After fusion settles, give every fused-output epilogue a real store pointer
  // (plus a pre-cast accumulation buffer for mixed-precision accumulation).
  pm.addNestedPass<GraphOp>(MAP::createAllocateAccumulatingBuffers());

  // An unfused reshape has no MAPToMOGG lowering (its hoisted stride op isn't
  // LowerableToMOGGInterface yet), and an unfused contiguous slice can take the
  // zero-copy path. Raise both back before outlining commits to MAP.
  pm.addNestedPass<GraphOp>(MAP::createRaiseBackContiguousViews());

  pm.addPass(MAP::createOutlineStructuredKernelBodies());
  // Uniques `map.iter.opaque` inputs and captures so the lowered kernel's
  // parameter list is minimal.
  pm.addNestedPass<GraphOp>(mlir::createCanonicalizerPass());
  pm.addNestedPass<GraphOp>(MAP::createLoopInvariantViewMotion());
  // CSE before canonicalize: two loads hoisting the same view create identical
  // stride ops; CSE must unify them so DedupeCapturingClosureCaptures can fold
  // the duplicate captures.
  pm.addNestedPass<GraphOp>(mlir::createCSEPass());
  pm.addNestedPass<GraphOp>(mlir::createCanonicalizerPass());
}

void M::MO::buildMoggPipeline(mlir::OpPassManager &pm,
                              const MoggPipelineOptions &) {
  pm.addPass(MOGG::createLegalizeRowwiseKernels());
  pm.addPass(MOGG::createConformCallOperands());
  pm.addPass(MOGG::createOutlineRoutines());
  pm.addPass(MOGG::createWrapFuncsWithTrace());

  // On the module, not GraphOp: the outlined stubs are its siblings.
  pm.addPass(mlir::createCanonicalizerPass());
  pm.addPass(mlir::createCSEPass());
}

void M::MO::buildMgpPipeline(mlir::OpPassManager &pm,
                             const MgpPipelineOptions &opts) {
  auto kernelLibraryPaths =
      llvm::to_vector_of<std::string>(opts.kernelLibraryPaths);

  pm.addNestedPass<MGP::ModelOp>(mlir::createCSEPass());
  pm.addNestedPass<MGP::ModelOp>(mlir::createCanonicalizerPass());
  pm.addPass(MGP::createSimplifyChainsPass());
  pm.addPass(MGP::createConcatInPlacePass());
  pm.addPass(MGP::createExecInvariantCodeMotionPass());

  // After ExecInvariantCodeMotion: buffer reuse can block hoisting.
  pm.addPass(MGP::createSimpleBufferReusePass());

  pm.addPass(MGP::createDynamicMemoryPlanningPass());
  pm.addPass(MGP::createDeferAllocsPass());
  pm.addPass(MGP::createVerifyModelArgumentsPass());
  pm.addPass(MGP::createPredicateAssertDependenciesPass());
  pm.addPass(MGP::createSimplifyChainsPass());
  pm.addNestedPass<MGP::ModelOp>(mlir::createCanonicalizerPass());
  pm.addNestedPass<MGP::ModelOp>(mlir::createCSEPass());

  // Before any fusion.
  pm.addPass(MGP::createAttachPythonStackTraces());

  pm.addPass(MGP::createGlobalizeSlotIndicesPass());
  pm.addNestedPass<MGP::ModelOp>(mlir::createCanonicalizerPass());
  pm.addNestedPass<MGP::ModelOp>(mlir::createCSEPass());

  MGP::LowerPrimitivesOptions lowerPrimOpts;
  lowerPrimOpts.kernelLibraryPaths = kernelLibraryPaths;
  lowerPrimOpts.minimumCpuAlignment = opts.minimumCpuAlignment;
  pm.addPass(MGP::createLowerPrimitives(lowerPrimOpts));

  {
    pm.addPass(MGP::createStageDeviceGraphsPass());
    pm.addPass(MGP::createPartitionDeviceGraphCollectivePass());
    pm.addPass(MGP::createComputeDeviceGraphDependenciesPass());
    pm.addNestedPass<MGP::ModelOp>(mlir::createCanonicalizerPass());
    pm.addPass(MGP::createSimplifyDeviceGraphDependenciesPass());
    pm.addNestedPass<MGP::ModelOp>(mlir::createCanonicalizerPass());
    pm.addNestedPass<MGP::ModelOp>(mlir::createCSEPass());
    pm.addPass(MGP::createGenerateBuildGraphStubsPass());
    // Drop the dead launch context chain before finalization audits the
    // builder bridge's live users.
    pm.addNestedPass<MGP::ModelOp>(mlir::createCanonicalizerPass());
    pm.addPass(MGP::createFinalizeDeviceGraphsPass());
    pm.addPass(mlir::createReconcileUnrealizedCastsPass());
  }

  pm.addPass(MOGG::createSequenceFusion());
  pm.addNestedPass<MGP::ModelOp>(mlir::createCanonicalizerPass());
  pm.addPass(MGP::createSimplifyChainsPass());
  pm.addNestedPass<MGP::ModelOp>(mlir::createCanonicalizerPass());
  pm.addNestedPass<MGP::ModelOp>(mlir::createCSEPass());

  pm.addPass(MGP::createSimplifyExtendLifetimesPass());

  pm.addPass(MOGG::createOutlineAsyncRoutines());
  pm.addPass(MOGG::createLookupConstantResources());

  // Lifting slot-index constants into stub arguments lets kernels differing
  // only in those indices merge below.
  pm.addPass(MOGG::createLiftBufferCacheSlots());

  // The emitted Mojo reads neither device ids nor symbolic dim names, so
  // erasing them lets per-device and per-layer copies merge below.
  pm.addPass(MOGG::createCanonicalizeFuncsForMerge());

  // Stubs that differ only by a redundant op merge once it is gone.
  pm.addPass(mlir::createCanonicalizerPass());
  pm.addPass(mlir::createCSEPass());
  pm.addPass(MOGG::createMergeIdenticalFuncs());

  // index.constant emits fewer lines of Mojo than its lowered form.
  pm.addPass(MGP::createRaiseBackIndexConstant());

  pm.addPass(MGP::createFixupOverhangsPass());
  pm.addNestedPass<MOGG::FuncOp>(mlir::createCanonicalizerPass());

  // Drop stubs orphaned by MergeIdenticalFuncs.
  pm.addPass(mlir::createSymbolDCEPass());

  // Before try/except wrapping: the begin/end Trace calls raise, and the
  // MGP-ABI entry point must not.
  if (opts.enableProfileScopeTracing) {
    MOGG::AddProfileScopeTracingOptions profileScopeOptions;
    profileScopeOptions.profileScopeTracingTraceUnlabelled =
        opts.profileScopeTracingTraceUnlabelled;
    pm.addPass(MOGG::createAddProfileScopeTracing(profileScopeOptions));
  }

  // Last, so it sees the final raising set; try/except around non-raising
  // code warns in the Mojo compiler.
  pm.addPass(MOGG::createAddTryExceptBlocks());

  MOGG::EmitMojoOptions emitMojoOptions;
  emitMojoOptions.kernelLibraryPaths = kernelLibraryPaths;
  emitMojoOptions.enableOpTraceComments = opts.enableOpTraceComments;
  emitMojoOptions.enableComputeLambdas = opts.enableComputeLambdas;
  emitMojoOptions.moggDebugDumpFusedTensorSpecs =
      opts.moggDebugDumpFusedTensorSpecs;
  pm.addPass(MOGG::createEmitMojo(emitMojoOptions));

  if (opts.dumpMojoText)
    pm.addPass(MOGG::createDumpMojo());
}

/// Appends every gc-pipeline stage to `pm`. With `dumpIntermediates`, a
/// DumpStagePass runs before the first stage and after each one.
static void gcPipelineImpl(mlir::OpPassManager &pm,
                           const GCPipelineOptions &opts, bool skipJit,
                           bool dumpIntermediates) {

  auto kernelLibraryPaths =
      llvm::to_vector_of<std::string>(opts.kernelLibraryPaths);

  // Filled by the first ("mo") dump from the non-subgraph model names while
  // the GraphOps still exist; later dumps reuse it.
  auto dumpBaseName = std::make_shared<std::string>();

  if (dumpIntermediates)
    pm.addPass(MO::createDumpStagePass("mo", dumpBaseName));

  MoPipelineOptions moOpts;
  moOpts.debugPrintAllTensors = opts.debugPrintAllTensors;
  moOpts.useShapeInference = opts.useShapeInference;
  moOpts.constantFold = opts.constantFold;
  if (opts.compiledFrameworkLabel.hasValue())
    moOpts.compiledFrameworkLabel = opts.compiledFrameworkLabel.getValue();
  if (opts.cacheDir.hasValue())
    moOpts.cacheDir = opts.cacheDir.getValue();
  moOpts.symbolicFfastMath = opts.symbolicFfastMath;
  moOpts.symbolicNoUndefinedMath = opts.symbolicNoUndefinedMath;
  moOpts.kernelLibraryPaths = kernelLibraryPaths;
  moOpts.kernelDeclsPrePopulated = opts.kernelDeclsPrePopulated;
  moOpts.usePatterns = opts.usePatterns;
  moOpts.patternFusionMHAEnable = opts.patternFusionMHAEnable;
  moOpts.patternFusionMHAAllowUnsafeBCasts =
      opts.patternFusionMHAAllowUnsafeBCasts;
  moOpts.patternFusionMHAAllowInternalReshape =
      opts.patternFusionMHAAllowInternalReshape;
  moOpts.sanityCheckShapeFuncs = opts.sanityCheckShapeFuncs;
  moOpts.defaultDeviceLabel = opts.defaultDeviceLabel;
  moOpts.defaultDeviceId = opts.defaultDeviceId;
  moOpts.defaultDeviceTargetTriple = opts.defaultDeviceTargetTriple;
  moOpts.defaultDeviceTargetArch = opts.defaultDeviceTargetArch;
  moOpts.fuseJitKernels = opts.fuseJitKernels;

  MapPipelineOptions mapOpts;
  mapOpts.fuseMutableLoadStore = opts.fuseMutableLoadStore;

  MoggPipelineOptions moggOpts;

  MGP::MOGGToMGPOptions moToPrimOpts;
  moToPrimOpts.minimumCpuAlignment = opts.minimumCpuAlignment;
  if (opts.compiledFrameworkLabel.hasValue())
    moToPrimOpts.compiledFrameworkLabel = opts.compiledFrameworkLabel;

  MgpPipelineOptions mgpOpts;
  mgpOpts.kernelLibraryPaths = kernelLibraryPaths;
  mgpOpts.minimumCpuAlignment = opts.minimumCpuAlignment;
  mgpOpts.enableOpTraceComments = opts.enableOpTraceComments;
  mgpOpts.enableComputeLambdas = opts.enableComputeLambdas;
  mgpOpts.moggDebugDumpFusedTensorSpecs = opts.moggDebugDumpFusedTensorSpecs;
  mgpOpts.dumpMojoText = opts.dumpMojoText;
  mgpOpts.enableProfileScopeTracing = opts.enableProfileScopeTracing;
  mgpOpts.profileScopeTracingTraceUnlabelled =
      opts.profileScopeTracingTraceUnlabelled;

  MOGG::JitCompileKernelsOptions jitOpts;
  if (!skipJit) {
    jitOpts.minimumCpuAlignment = opts.minimumCpuAlignment;
    jitOpts.saveTempPrefix = opts.saveTempPrefix;
    jitOpts.createMOGGReproducers = opts.createMOGGReproducers;
    jitOpts.kernelLibraryPaths = kernelLibraryPaths;
    jitOpts.timeMOGGCompile = opts.timeMOGGCompile;
    jitOpts.debugKGENStubs = opts.debugKGENStubs;
    // Cross-compile for the requested GPU instead of probing the host.
    jitOpts.defaultDeviceTargetArch = opts.defaultDeviceTargetArch;
    jitOpts.defaultDeviceTargetTriple = opts.defaultDeviceTargetTriple;
    jitOpts.compileForHostExecution = opts.compileForHostExecution;
  }

  auto buildStage = [&](auto &&build, const std::string &dumpSuffix) {
    build(pm);
    if (dumpIntermediates && !dumpSuffix.empty())
      pm.addPass(MO::createDumpStagePass(dumpSuffix, dumpBaseName));
  };

  buildStage([&](auto &p) { buildMoPipeline(p, moOpts); }, "mo-pre-map");

  // Stable-tensor marking must see MO ops, so it runs as the last MO-level
  // pass before the dialect is lowered away.
  buildStage(
      [&](auto &p) {
        p.addPass(MO::createMarkStableTensorsPass());
        p.addPass(MO::createMOToMAP());
      },
      "mo-to-map");

  buildStage(
      [&](auto &p) {
        buildMapPipeline(p, mapOpts);
        // After MAP fusion so a check never fuses into the kernel it checks;
        // before map-to-mogg so the injected checks compile with the rest.
        if (opts.nanCheck)
          p.addPass(MO::createNanCheckPass(opts.nanCheckStride));
      },
      "map-pre-mogg");

  MAP::MAPToMOGGOptions mapToMoggOpts;
  mapToMoggOpts.enableComputeLambdas = opts.enableComputeLambdas;
  buildStage([&](auto &p) { p.addPass(MAP::createMAPToMOGG(mapToMoggOpts)); },
             "map-to-mogg");

  buildStage(
      [&](auto &p) {
        buildMoggPipeline(p, moggOpts);
        // OpaqueLoc tracebacks can't be printed, so convert them for the
        // dump. Dump-only: this strips the OpaqueLocs buildMgpPipeline's
        // assert handling reads.
        if (dumpIntermediates)
          p.addPass(MGP::createAttachPythonStackTraces());
      },
      "mogg-pre-mgp");

  buildStage([&](auto &p) { p.addPass(MGP::createMOGGToMGP(moToPrimOpts)); },
             "mogg-to-mgp");

  buildStage(
      [&](auto &p) {
        buildMgpPipeline(p, mgpOpts);
        if (!skipJit) {
          p.addPass(MOGG::createJitCompileKernels(jitOpts));
          p.addPass(MOGG::createStripKernelDecls());
          buildJitPipeline(p);
        }
      },
      "mgp");
}

} // namespace

void M::MO::buildGCPipeline(mlir::OpPassManager &pm,
                            const GCPipelineOptions &opts) {
  gcPipelineImpl(pm, opts, /*skipJit=*/false);
}

void M::MO::buildGCPipelineThroughEmitMojo(mlir::OpPassManager &pm,
                                           const GCPipelineOptions &opts) {
  gcPipelineImpl(pm, opts, /*skipJit=*/true);
}

LogicalResult M::MO::runGCPipeline(ModuleOp moduleOp,
                                   const GCPipelineOptions &opts,
                                   bool dumpIntermediates) {
  auto pm = mlir::PassManager::on<ModuleOp>(
      moduleOp.getContext(), mlir::OpPassManager::Nesting::Implicit);

  if (!opts.mlirTimingOutDir.empty()) {
    auto enabledTiming = M::configureMLIRPassTimingJSONOutput(
        pm, opts.mlirTimingOutDir.getValue(), "GC Pipeline");
    if (enabledTiming.isError()) {
      llvm::errs() << enabledTiming.getError() << "\n";
      return failure();
    }
  }

  gcPipelineImpl(pm, opts, /*skipJit=*/opts.preJit, dumpIntermediates);
  return pm.run(moduleOp);
}

void M::MO::buildShapeInferencePipeline(mlir::OpPassManager &pm) {
  // Turns static reshapes like `[D0] -> [1]` into rebinds (so staticization
  // needn't look through them) and materializes parameter definitions for
  // `mo.rebind`s that still declare output parameters.
  pm.addNestedPass<MO::GraphOp>(mlir::createCanonicalizerPass());

  // Evaluates constant ops and shape functions in the parameter domain, then
  // simplifies parameter bindings by substitution and constraint solving.
  pm.addNestedPass<MO::GraphOp>(MO::createPropagateShapes());
  pm.addNestedPass<MO::GraphOp>(mlir::createCSEPass());
  pm.addNestedPass<MO::GraphOp>(mlir::createCanonicalizerPass());
  pm.addPass(KGEN::createVerifyParameters());
}

using BlobMap = DenseMap<const uint8_t *, mlir::AsmResourceBlob *>;

static BlobMap getDenseResources(ModuleOp module) {
  BlobMap result;
  for (Operation &op : module.getOps()) {
    if (auto modelOp = dyn_cast<MGP::ModelOp>(op)) {
      modelOp.walk([&](MGP::BufferConstantOp constOp) {
        auto elementsAttr = constOp.getValue();
        if (auto resourceAttr =
                dyn_cast<DenseResourceElementsAttr>(elementsAttr)) {
          mlir::AsmResourceBlob *blob = resourceAttr.getRawHandle().getBlob();
          if (blob->getDeleter())
            result[blob->getDataAs<uint8_t>().data()] = blob;
        }
      });
    }
  }

  return result;
}

ErrorOr<BufferRef> M::MO::convertMGPToMEF(ModuleOp module,
                                          bool enableMEFMetadata) {
  OwningOpRef<ModuleOp> moduleToRewrite = module.clone();
  // Device-generic ops get renamed with their device label so GraphRT can
  // dispatch to a device-appropriate primitive.
  BlobMap resources = getDenseResources(*moduleToRewrite);
  mlir::PassManager pm = mlir::PassManager::on<ModuleOp>(
      module->getContext(), mlir::OpPassManager::Nesting::Implicit);
  pm.addPass(MGP::createPrepareDevicePrimitivesPass());
  FormatScopedDiagnosticHandler diagnostics(moduleToRewrite->getContext());
  if (failed(pm.run(*moduleToRewrite)))
    return Error(Twine("Failed to prepare MGP model for conversion to MEF. ") +
                 diagnostics.formatMessage());
  ConcatenationTree result =
      translateMLIRToMEF(*moduleToRewrite, enableMEFMetadata);
  if (result.getSize() == 0) {
    return Error(Twine("Failed to convert model to MEF. ") +
                 diagnostics.formatMessage());
  }
  M::WriteableBufferRef outputBuffer = WriteableBuffer::get(
      0, maxAttributeAlignment().value(), result.getSize());
  result.traverse([&](ArrayRef<uint8_t> data) {
    outputBuffer->write(reinterpret_cast<const char *>(data.data()),
                        data.size());
    if (resources.count(data.data())) {
      if (auto blob = resources[data.data()]; blob->getDeleter()) {
        // Free owned blob data as soon as it's been copied out.
        auto ref = M::GML::BlobLifetimeManager(std::move(blob->getDeleter()),
                                               blob->getData(),
                                               blob->getDataAlignment());
        blob->getDeleter() = nullptr;
      }
    }
  });

  return outputBuffer;
}
